text: {"observations":"Evidence is indirect but points to a choir. Texture is very tonal (noisiness 0-2) with only 13 weak onsets in 10 s and no steady percussion or plucked attacks. Several sustained pitches sound together across about three octaves, e.g. 6.6-7.3 s: 74, 110, 146, 183, 219, 293, 368, 439, 587 Hz (a spread D major chord at similar levels), and 2.7-3.3 s: 123, 184, 246, 368, 492 Hz. The lines move slowly and stepwise with voice-like glides (about 250 to 278 Hz at 3.5-3.8 s, 327 to 369 Hz at 0.2-0.45 s, 246 to 221 Hz at 9.2-9.4 s). Irregular bursts of 4-8 kHz noise at about 6.5, 8.7-9.0 and 9.7 s look like sibilant consonants, so voices are present, which argues against D. There is no single dominant line with vibrato or strong 2-4 kHz presence (that region is 30-45 dB down), which argues against a solo male (A) or female (B) lead; simultaneous sung parts from bass to soprano range fit C.","answer":"C"}
